transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I'm just really struggling with how horrible my skin looks. I have these awful acne scars and blemishes all over my face, and I feel so ugly and deformed. I just can't bear how terrible it looks.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time checking your skin in the mirror, trying to hide or fix it, or comparing your appearance to others?

Yes, I spend hours staring in the mirror and picking at my skin to try and 'fix' it, which usually just makes it worse. I also use heavy makeup to hide it and constantly compare my face to everyone I see, which is honestly exhausting and depressing.

  "category": "differential point",

Yes, my family and friends constantly tell me they don't see anything and that I look completely normal. But I'm just so insecure and convinced the flaws are obvious that I can't help but ask them for reassurance over and over again.
Outside of your concerns about your skin, have you been feeling down, depressed, or lost interest in your usual activities for most of the day, nearly every day?

No, I haven't really been feeling depressed or lost interest in my usual activities overall. Almost all of my distress and worry is focused entirely on my skin concerns. If my face didn't look like this, I think I would be completely fine.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were Body Dysmorphic Disorder and Major Depressive Disorder. Based on this conversation, Major Depressive Disorder is unlikely because the patient explicitly denied experiencing generalized depressive symptoms or loss of interest in activities, stating their distress is entirely focused on their skin concerns. The patient's symptoms of preoccupation with perceived physical flaws, repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, skin picking, reassurance seeking), and significant distress align perfectly with Body Dysmorphic Disorder.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a severe preoccupation with perceived physical flaws (acne scars and blemishes) that are unnoticeable to others, accompanied by repetitive behaviors such as excessive mirror checking, skin picking, reassurance-seeking, and camouflaging. These symptoms are highly characteristic of Body Dysmorphic Disorder and cause significant distress, while other primary psychiatric conditions like Major Depressive Disorder have been ruled out.
